proof:
Source: steps 7 and 8 of the parent proof (compactness and limit equation) together with the subsequence extraction of A_k = ah_k(0) and e_k. The proof uses the sibling lemmas holder_diag_subseq, c1_limit and weak_eq_limit.
1. Frozen coefficients. By (d), |ah_k(0)[P][Q]| <= max(M, 0) ||P|| ||Q||. Hence the bilinear operator norm satisfies ||ah_k(0)|| <= max(M, 0) (ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound₂). Bil is a finite-dimensional normed space, so it is proper. By Bolzano-Weierstrass (tendsto_subseq_of_bounded) there are a strictly increasing phi_A and A in Bil with ah_{phi_A(j)}(0) -> A in operator norm. (Lean: FiniteDimensional, ProperSpace, the norm and subtraction on Bil are only synthesized with `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3` at tactic level.)
2. Unit vectors. The points e_{phi_A(j)} lie in Bbar_1(0). By Bolzano-Weierstrass in R^n there are a strictly increasing phi_e and e0 with e_{phi_A(phi_e(j))} -> e0. Put phi_1 := phi_A o phi_e, which is strictly increasing.
3. Apply holder_diag_subseq to f_j := DW_{phi_1(j)} with radii R_{phi_1(j)}, exponent alpha > 0 and constant K >= 0.
 a. Hypotheses: R_{phi_1(j)} -> infinity because phi_1(j) -> infinity; f_j(0) = 0 and the Hoelder bound on B_{R_{phi_1(j)}}(0) hold by (b).
 b. It gives a strictly increasing phi_2 and V : R^n -> L such that V(0) = 0, V is continuous, and ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z'.
 c. With psi := phi_1 o phi_2 (strictly increasing), DW_{psi(i)} -> V uniformly on Bbar_r(0) for every real r.
4. Apply c1_limit to W_{psi(i)} with radii R_{psi(i)} and V. Its hypotheses hold by (b) and step 3. It yields W : R^n -> R^l, C^1 on R^n, with DW(z) = V(z) for all z. Hence ||DW(z) - DW(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z', and DW(0) = V(0) = 0.
5. Coefficient bound for the limit equation.
 a. Along psi, ah_{psi(i)}(0) -> A, being a subsequence of the sequence of step 1. So eps_i := ||ah_{psi(i)}(0) - A|| -> 0.
 b. For all P, Q: |ah_{psi(i)}(0)[P][Q] - A[P][Q]| <= eps_i ||P|| ||Q||.
 c. For z in B_{R_{psi(i)}}(0), (e) gives |ah_{psi(i)}(z)[P][Q] - A[P][Q]| <= c_{psi(i)} |z|^alpha ||P|| ||Q|| + eps_i ||P|| ||Q|| <= c'_i (1 + |z|^alpha) ||P|| ||Q||, where c'_i := |c_{psi(i)}| + eps_i -> 0.
6. Apply weak_eq_limit with A, ah_{psi(i)}, Psi_{psi(i)}, U_i := DW_{psi(i)}, V, radii R_{psi(i)}, constants c'_i and d_{psi(i)}, and the exponent alpha >= 0. Its hypotheses hold:
 a. R_{psi(i)} -> infinity, c'_i -> 0 and d_{psi(i)} -> 0.
 b. V is continuous, and U_i -> V uniformly on every Bbar_r(0) by step 3.
 c. The joint continuity of ah_{psi(i)} and the continuity of Psi_{psi(i)} hold by (c). U_i is continuous on B_{R_{psi(i)}}(0) because W_{psi(i)} is C^1 on that open ball.
 d. The coefficient bound is step 5, the bound on Psi is (e), and the weak equations are (f).
 Hence the integral of A[V][Dzeta] is 0, that is, the integral over R^n of A[DW][Dzeta] is 0, for every C^1_c map zeta.
7. Legendre bounds for A. For fixed P, Q, step 5b gives ah_{psi(i)}(0)[P][Q] -> A[P][Q]. Passing to the limit in (d) gives lam ||P||^2 <= A[P][P] and |A[P][Q]| <= M ||P|| ||Q||.
8. Unit gradient. e_{psi(i)} -> e0 with e_{psi(i)} in Bbar_1(0). DW_{psi(i)} -> V uniformly on Bbar_1(0) and V is continuous, so DW_{psi(i)}(e_{psi(i)}) -> V(e0) (TendstoUniformlyOn.tendsto_comp). By (g), and since psi(i) -> infinity, ||DW_{psi(i)}(e_{psi(i)})|| = 1 for all large i. Hence ||DW(e0)|| = ||V(e0)|| = 1.
9. Conclusion. Steps 4, 6, 7 and 8 give A and W with all the required properties. QED.
